findings.title: Empty skin_family_scope array bypasses template-set family gate
findings.why_it_matters: When a template set's skin_family_scope is [] (empty array), templateScope is built as an empty Set (size === 0). The guard condition `templateScope && templateScope.size && !templateScope.has(skinFamily)` short-circuits on `templateScope.size` (falsy zero) and skips the family restriction entirely. Any skin family that passes the other checks will be treated as in-scope. A future template set added to the JSON without an explicit skin_family_scope list would expose all skin families to authoring — including proof_only families if the server-side familyScope check is also missing — rather than being fail-closed.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat an empty templateScope as unrestricted ONLY if the JSON field is absent (null templateScope). If the array is present but empty, treat it as 'no families allowed' — i.e. `if (templateScope !== null && (!templateScope.size || !templateScope.has(skinFamily))) return false;`.
evidence: Line 7003-7005: `const templateScope = Array.isArray(ts?.skin_family_scope) ? new Set(...) : null`. An empty array [] produces a Set with size 0.

Line 7006: `if (templateScope && templateScope.size && !templateScope.has(skinFamily)) return false;` — when size is 0, the middle operand is falsy, so the entire condition is false and the return is never reached.

Consequence: a template set with `skin_family_scope: []` would skip the template-level family check and fall through to the familyScope and prefixSpec checks. If both pass (e.g. for a future authorable family), the action is presented as authorable despite the intent of scope: [].
The current JSON uses non-empty arrays so this does not fire today, but the invariant is fragile.

findings.title: Stale empty-registry cached when file missing at first call
findings.why_it_matters: load_template_registry() checks `if not reg_path.exists()` and, when the file is absent, writes `_template_registry = {'template_sets': {}, 'schema_version': 2}` and returns. This value is the sentinel for 'already loaded'. On all subsequent calls the global is not None, so the early-return fires and the empty stub is returned forever — even after the file is deployed. In a Cloud Run cold-start race where the config file is mounted from a volume that hasn't finished initializing, any request that arrives in the first few milliseconds will permanently poison the registry cache for the lifetime of that instance. The only recovery is a process restart.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not cache the empty-stub result. Either return it without assigning to _template_registry, or use a separate sentinel to distinguish 'file truly absent' from 'not yet loaded'.
evidence: Line 1086-1091: `if _template_registry is not None: return _template_registry`. If file is missing, `_template_registry = {'template_sets': {}, 'schema_version': 2}` is stored and returned.
Every subsequent call to load_template_registry() finds _template_registry is not None and returns the empty stub.
The same instance is mutated by the caller in app.py (previously `reg['enabled_families'] = ...`) — the diff removes that mutation but the caching behaviour is unchanged.

Concrete scenario: Cloud Run mounts config/ via a secret volume. Container starts, first HTTP request arrives at /api/workbench/templates before the volume is ready. File is missing → empty stub cached. Volume becomes available 200 ms later. All subsequent requests return empty registry. Workbench shows 0 actions until next instance restart.

findings.title: preview_xp silently inherits l0_ref value producing mismatched preview
findings.why_it_matters: _resolve_preview_xp_fields() falls back to l0_ref when preview_xp is absent. preview_xp is described as a frame-1 sprite; l0_ref is a fully-assembled 100-frame reference sheet. They are different files serving different display purposes. If someone adds a new action entry to the JSON and omits preview_xp but includes l0_ref, normalization silently substitutes the 100-frame sheet as the preview. No error is raised, no warning is logged, and the field name preview_xp in the output now points to a file whose content is semantically wrong for preview display. The drift validation cross-checks prefix_catalog vs template_set fields, but both sides go through the same normalization so both sides would carry the same wrong path — drift detection passes, the silent corruption propagates.
findings.suggested_fix: Log a warning when the fallback fires so that new entries without explicit preview_xp are visible at load time. Optionally require preview_xp to be explicitly set and treat the fallback as a schema migration path only.
evidence: Lines 970-974 (service.py): _resolve_preview_xp_fields returns l0_ref/l0_ref_sha256 as the preview pair whenever preview_xp is absent.
Lines 994-996: the validation check `if not preview_xp: missing.append('preview_xp')` runs AFTER the fallback has already populated preview_xp, so it never fires when l0_ref is present.

Example: add action with only l0_ref='sprites/player-0100.xp' (100 frames). After normalization: preview_xp='sprites/player-0100.xp'. Frontend uses this as the action thumbnail — wrong frame count, wrong file.

Drift validator at line 1070-1077 compares prefix_catalog preview_xp against action_spec preview_xp. Since prefix_catalog spec goes through the same normalization, both are set to l0_ref value. Drift check passes.

findings.title: Template linkage gate skipped when templateSetKey is empty string
findings.why_it_matters: The linkage check `if (templateActions.length && templateSetKey)` is skipped when templateSetKey is an empty string. state.templateSetKey is initialized as 'player_native_idle_only' but could be '' if another code path resets it (e.g. a failed template apply). When templateSetKey is empty, a prefix with a non-empty template_actions list still passes the linkage gate because templateSetKey is falsy. The action appears as authorable even though the current template context is undefined. The user could interact with action tabs from a previous bundle context while state.templateSetKey no longer reflects a valid template.
findings.suggested_fix: When templateSetKey is empty and templateActions is non-empty, return false rather than skipping the check. An unknown template context cannot be linked.
evidence: Line 188: `templateSetKey: 'player_native_idle_only'` initial state.
Line 7017: `const templateSetKey = String(state.templateSetKey || '').trim();`
Line 7019: `if (templateActions.length && templateSetKey)` — if templateSetKey is '' after a reset, this evaluates to false and the linkage check is skipped entirely.
Line 7334: Inside applyCurrentTemplate, state.templateSetKey is set from the select element value. If the value is '' (element missing or reset), templateSetKey becomes '' permanently.
With templateSetKey='', a prefix like 'player' that has template_actions=[{template_set_key:'player_native_full', action_key:'idle'}] would still return true from isTemplateActionAuthorable.

findings.title: Drift validation checks only first matching template_action per prefix
findings.why_it_matters: A prefix can appear in multiple template sets (e.g. 'player' appears in both player_native_idle_only and player_native_full). The drift validation loop iterates over all template_actions entries for each prefix and validates fields against each referenced action. However, the fields being compared are the top-level prefix_catalog fields (filename_prefix, skin_family, preview_xp, etc.) against the action_spec fields. For the 'player' prefix, preview_xp is 'player-0001.xp' in both template sets, so no drift is detected today. But if two linked template sets ever define different preview_xp values for what is notionally the same prefix action (e.g. action 'idle' in two different template sets with different pixel resolutions), the drift validator would raise for the second template set entry because the prefix_catalog can only store one canonical preview_xp. The validator does not tell the author which template_action to align to — it fails with an opaque drift error.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that prefix_catalog preview fields are canonical for the prefix regardless of template set. The validator is correct; improve the error message to name both the prefix and the offending template_set_key.
evidence: Lines 1050-1077: for each template_action entry in prefix_catalog, the loop validates 6 fields of ps (prefix spec) against action_spec (the normalized template action).
'player' has two template_action entries pointing to player_native_idle_only:idle and player_native_full:idle. Both are validated against the same ps dict.
If player_native_idle_only:idle and player_native_full:idle ever diverge in preview_xp, the validator would raise — but the error message does not identify which template_action caused the conflict.
The constraint that a prefix can only have one canonical preview_xp is implicit, not documented.

findings.title: Race: getEnabledActions called with stale null templateRegistry during async fetch
findings.why_it_matters: fetchTemplateRegistry() is async. Between page load and fetch completion, state.templateRegistry is null. Several synchronous code paths call getEnabledActions(ts) directly without waiting: renderBundleActionTabs() (line 7173), updateBundleUI() (line 7272), areAllEnabledBundleActionsReady() (line 7068), applyCurrentXpAsWebSkin() (line 1357), testCurrentSkinInDock() (line 1510). Inside isTemplateActionAuthorable, line 7008 uses optional chaining: `state.templateRegistry?.skin_family_scope?.[skinFamily]` — this returns undefined, making familyScope falsy, and the function returns false. So all actions are hidden while the registry is loading. This is silently fail-closed rather than showing a loading state. More critically: if the fetch fails (network error, line 6985 catches and ignores), state.templateRegistry remains null permanently and the UI shows zero actions forever with no error message visible from this path.
findings.suggested_fix: Surface a user-visible error in getEnabledActions or its callers when state.templateRegistry is null and the fetch is known to have failed. The catch on line 6985 discards the error silently.
evidence: Line 6985: `catch (_e) { /* ignore */ }` — any fetch failure leaves state.templateRegistry null.
Line 6986: returns state.templateRegistry which is null.
Line 7008: `const familyScope = state.templateRegistry?.skin_family_scope?.[skinFamily]` — if state.templateRegistry is null, familyScope is undefined.
Line 7009: `if (!familyScope || ...)  return false;` — returns false for every action.

Lines 7272, 7173, 1357, 1510: these callers don't await fetchTemplateRegistry before calling getEnabledActions. If they're triggered (e.g. by state restoration or hot-key) before the fetch resolves, they silently get an empty action set.

findings.title: prefix_catalog authorable false overrides skin_family authorable true silently
findings.why_it_matters: The gate checks familyScope.authorable AND prefixSpec.authorable independently. A prefix can be authorable=false while its skin_family is authorable=true (wolfie, wolack, bigbee are all skin_family='human' but authorable=false). This is correctly handled. However the reverse — skin_family authorable=false while a specific prefix is authorable=true — is also correctly blocked by the familyScope check at line 7009. The issue is that there is no user-visible feedback explaining WHY a specific prefix was blocked; debugging requires reading both the familyScope and prefixSpec. This is a UX/diagnostics gap, not a correctness bug. Flagged as P3 because future debugging sessions during registry expansion will be time-consuming.
evidence: Line 7009: familyScope check fires first. If authorable=false, returns false regardless of prefixSpec.
Line 7015: prefixSpec.authorable check fires second. If false, returns false.
No log statement distinguishes between the two rejection reasons.
For wolfie: familyScope (human) is authorable=true, but prefixSpec.authorable=false. The function reaches line 7015 and returns false with no log.

residual_risks: The global _template_registry module-level variable is shared across all Flask requests in the same worker process. Flask's development server is single-threaded; gunicorn with multiple threads or gevent workers could create a race between the None check (line 1086) and the assignment (line 1092). Python's GIL makes this unlikely with standard threading but not impossible under gevent patching.

ENABLED_FAMILIES in config.py (line 38) still exists and is exported. Although app.py no longer appends it to the registry response, it remains importable. Any code path that independently imports and uses ENABLED_FAMILIES will apply the old gating logic alongside the new multi-gate check — creating divergent authorization.

The drift validator compares prefix_catalog fields against normalized action specs. The normalization aliases 'family' = filename_prefix. If a future action spec defines 'family' with a different value than 'filename_prefix', _normalize_template_action_spec will use filename_prefix (checked first at line 983) and overwrite family. The drift check then compares against the overwritten value, potentially masking a real divergence in the original JSON.

bundle_contract.mjs now reads skin_family_scope from template sets. If a template set lacks this field, getTemplateSetContract returns `skin_family_scope: []`. The empty array semantics in bundle_contract.mjs (a separate execution context from workbench.js) may be interpreted differently by fidelity tests than by the workbench UI — neither documents the intended semantics of an empty scope list.
testing_gaps: No test covers isTemplateActionAuthorable when state.templateRegistry is null — specifically that all actions are hidden (fail-closed) rather than all visible (fail-open).
No test constructs a template set with skin_family_scope: [] and verifies that no families are authorized (the current code would allow all families through the template-scope check).

No test covers the file-absent race: load_template_registry() called when file is missing, then called again after the file appears — verifying whether the second call returns the real registry or the cached stub.
No test covers templateSetKey='' in isTemplateActionAuthorable with a prefix that has non-empty template_actions.

test_template_registry_actions_are_normalized (line 577) hardcodes `action['skin_family'] == 'human'` — this test would pass even if the normalization were incorrectly allowing non-human families, because the assertion only validates the current fixture data.
